attributes.provenance: Discovered and fully diagnosed in game/world/gauntworld.c::fn_8005BA1C during work_claim.gauntworld-defake3.20260831.v1 (attempt.gauntworld-defake3-tupass.20260831.v1's reverted gWorldInfo sub-attempt). fn_8005BA1C has FOUR textually-identical `for (k = 0; k < *(s32*)(BASE + 0x74); k++)` loop headers (chicken/apple/gold/silver sub-cases) bounding an iteminfo-array walk off gWorldInfo. A block-local `u8* world = gWorldInfo;` is assigned once at the top of the case-2 block. The pre-existing byte-exact source used `world + 0x74` as BASE in the first two loop headers (chicken/apple) and the raw `gWorldInfo + 0x74` directly (bypassing the local) in the other two (gold/silver) - a genuine, deliberate-looking asymmetry despite `world` holding the identical address at every one of the four sites (no intervening reassignment). A mechanical `sed`-style unification of all four onto `world + 0x74` (justified at the time as 'these are the same value, harmless respelling for consistency') regressed fn_8005BA1C itself (real 529->615, STRUCTURAL: opcode multiset DIFFERS with extra bne/b pairs and li/addi shuffling - a register-liveness/branch-shape cascade) AND, independently and unexpectedly, regressed an ENTIRELY UNRELATED sibling function fn_8005FDA8 defined ~4000 source lines later in the same TU (real 16->62, lfs/lfd/fmuls pattern shift) which contains no reference to gWorldInfo, world, or anything in fn_8005BA1C. Reverting only the two wrongly-unified gold/silver sites back to the bare `gWorldInfo + 0x74` form (restoring the original per-site asymmetry exactly) fixed BOTH regressions simultaneously with no other change - conclusively proving the whole-TU coupling was a downstream consequence of fn_8005BA1C's own codegen shape/size changing, not a separate independent bug.
attributes.scope: MWCC GC 1.2.5 family; applies whenever a de-fakematch (or any source-shape) pass touches 2+ occurrences of numerically-identical access to the SAME global within one function, where some occurrences already route through an existing local pointer/copy holding that global's address and others reference the global symbol directly at that specific site.

subject: compiler:mwcc-gc-1.2.5
value: Within one function, when a global's address is available both directly (the symbol itself) and through an already-assigned local pointer copy, MWCC does NOT treat a direct symbol reference and a reload-from-local-register as interchangeable, even though both resolve to the identical runtime address and even at multiple sites that are textually/semantically identical to each other. Whichever form the ORIGINAL retail C source used at a GIVEN site is load-bearing for that site's instruction selection (address materialization choice, e.g. a fresh `lis/addi` pair vs reusing an already-live register) and can differ site-by-site within the same function for what looks like 'the same' access. Unifying such sites onto one spelling (even the objectively 'more consistent' one) is a genuine STRUCTURAL source-shape change, not a no-op respelling, and its effects are NOT confined to the edited function: changing one function's instruction count/shape shifts subsequent code's relationship to the TU's shared literal/constant pool (per AGENTS.md's general 'MWCC constant pools... create whole-TU coupling' warning), so a regression can surface in an unrelated SIBLING function later in the same TU that never references the touched global or local variable at all. Consequence: (1) when de-fakematching 2+ occurrences of one global's raw-offset access within a function, verify EACH site's existing base-pointer spelling (direct global vs local alias) individually before converting - never assume a single canonical form generalizes across all occurrences just because the computed addresses are provably equal; preserve whichever form was already there unless there is a specific reason (and verified evidence) to change it. (2) Any conversion that touches a widely-referenced global's access pattern should be gated against the FULL TU (defake_gate.py check on the whole file, or at minimum spot-check a few sibling functions), not just the directly-edited function - a clean gate on the touched function alone is not sufficient proof of no regression when a shared global or literal pool is involved.
